learning_objective: 🎯 Learn the accounting magic required when a new partner joins the firm! Calculate new profit shares, value the brand (goodwill), and revalue old assets.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: When a new partner joins, the old partners have to give up (sacrifice) a piece of their profit slice. The New Ratio shows how future profits will be divided among everyone.
The old partners worked hard for years to build the business's reputation. The new partner must pay them a 'Premium' in cash to compensate them for sacrificing a share of future profits.
Before the new partner enters, we must check the current market value of all assets and liabilities. Any profit or loss from this revaluation belongs ONLY to the old partners in their old ratio.
Any old savings, reserves (like General Reserve), or old losses sitting in the Balance Sheet must be emptied out and given to the old partners before the new partner steps in.

fun_activity.title: 🍰 The Sacrificing Slice
fun_activity.instructions: Draw a circle representing a pizza (total profit). Divide it in half for Partner A and B (1/2 each). A new Partner C joins for a 1/4th share. Erase 1/4th of the pizza. How much do A and B have left to share? You just calculated a Sacrificing Ratio!

exam_tips: 📌 Formula: Sacrificing Ratio = Old Ratio - New Ratio. The Premium for Goodwill is ALWAYS distributed among old partners in their Sacrificing Ratio, not the old ratio!
📌 If the new partner cannot bring Goodwill in cash, debit their Current Account (not Capital Account) so their core capital isn't reduced.
📌 Hidden Goodwill: If Total Firm's Capital (based on new partner's share) is GREATER than the combined actual capitals of all partners, the difference is Hidden Goodwill.
quick_recap: ⭐ Revaluation profit/loss is shared by OLD partners in OLD ratio.
⭐ Premium for Goodwill is shared by sacrificing partners in the SACRIFICING ratio.
⭐ Old reserves and old goodwill on the balance sheet are written off immediately.
